description: Implement a MyCalendar class to store events. A new event can be added if it does not cause a double booking. An event is represented as [start, end) (half-open interval). Return true if the event can be booked.
intuition: Think of a calendar as a sorted list of time intervals. A new event can be booked only if it does not overlap with any existing event. Binary search or linear scan through sorted intervals to check for conflicts before adding the new event.
approach: Maintain a sorted list of bookings. For each new event, check if it overlaps with any existing event. Two intervals [s1, e1) and [s2, e2) overlap if s1 < e2 and s2 < e1.
jsWalkthrough:
Operations: book(10,20), book(15,25), book(20,30)

book(10,20):
  No existing bookings → push [10,20]
  bookedIntervals=[[10,20]], return true

book(15,25):
  Check [10,20]: 15<20 AND 10<25 → OVERLAP → return false

book(20,30):
  Check [10,20]: 20<20? No → no overlap
  Push [20,30], return true
  bookedIntervals=[[10,20],[20,30]]
explanation:
1. Store all booked intervals in a list.
2. For a new event [start, end), check overlap with all existing events.
3. Two events overlap if start < existing_end and existing_start < end.
4. If no overlap, add the event and return True.
hints: Two half-open intervals overlap if and only if start1 < end2 and start2 < end1.
Check each existing booking for overlap before adding.
A balanced BST or SortedList can improve to O(log n) per booking.
